subject: Platform health & owner alignment — Sep checkpoint
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ops@orbitcloud.com
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Platform health & owner alignment — Sep checkpoint

Team — attaching the September snapshot and a short action matrix (attached). High-level notes: 

- Latency: P95 across hosted API is up 8% month-over-month; two short spikes (see latency-spike-log-2026-09.csv). Spikes correlate with batched resends from a single high-traffic tenant.
- Cost: Unit token cost drift ~+6% vs baseline; appears tied to longer-sequence requests and fallback to fp16 variant.
- Uptime: 99.90% for the month; one 18-minute region failover on 09/02 (brief runbook outage).
- Usage: Overall tokens +14% (healthy), but traffic concentration in three customers.

As we prep for QBR next week, I need: 
1) Owner confirmations for each line in the attached owner-action-matrix-2026-09.pdf (owners pre-filled; confirm or reassign).
2) A short (one-paragraph) explanation from each owner of what they’ll present for QBR on cost and latency mitigations.
3) Any gotchas we should surface to leadership (e.g., expected regressions, rollout risks).

Laura — can you pull the small sample of KV-cache vs non-cache traces for the spike tenant? Vivek — can you confirm whether we can reallocate two dedicated GPUs from a low-priority pool for a 48-hour repro window? Kim — please validate the cost delta numbers and whether quantization profiles explain the drift.

I’ll consolidate owners’ paragraphs into a single QBR slide and circulate before Fri EOD.

Thanks,
Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Sr. PM, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sep-platform-dashboard-2026.xlsx (spreadsheet), latency-spike-log-2026-09.csv (csv), owner-action-matrix-2026-09.pdf (pdf)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ops@orbitcloud.com
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Platform health & owner alignment — Sep checkpoint

Thanks Lukas — received and skimmed the dashboard. Quick answers:

- I grabbed KV-cache/non-cache traces for the tenant showing spikes and uploaded a 30MB sample to Drive (link in Confluence). Early look: cache misses spiked during the tenant's multi-worker migration window at 03:21 UTC on 09/02.
- For the QBR paragraph: I'll write that we observed brief cache warmup regressions during tenant-side rollout and outline the short remediation (prefetching + throttled fanout).

Question for Vivek: the owner-action-matrix suggests a 48h repro window that needs 2 gpus; if we reallocate resources do we need a regional plan (e.g., move from us-west to us-east)? If so, we should note the potential penalty to latency for small-number customers.

I'll confirm owners by EOD and attach the short paragraph.

Laura Bennett
Head of Observability
Redwood Inference

Lukas / team — we can spare 2xA10 GPUs from the dedicated low-priority pool for the 48-hour repro window. Conditions:

- Reserve window: 2026-09-13 00:00 UTC -> 2026-09-15 00:00 UTC (we should pick hours outside the tenant's peak if possible).
- Ops will require a short banner and fallback policy for the affected region during repro.
- If we do region move (us-west -> us-east) expect +12–18ms median latency for the affected customers; call this out in your QBR note.

Action: I'm assigning INF-4832 for scheduling; Ops will confirm 48 hours before start.

Vivek Kulkarni

For the QBR: Maria Santos (cc'ed) will join the 30-minute slot to speak to mitigations and the proposed prefetch patch.
